headline: ALL 5 HOLES HIT HIGH-GRADE — Graycliff's Shakespeare Returns 115 g/t Au Over 6m; Stock Jumps 31%
snippet: Graycliff Exploration (CSE: GRAY) reported that all five of its latest drill holes at the Shakespeare Gold Project in Ontario returned high-grade mineralization on November 5, with the best intercept hitting 115.25 g/t gold over 6 metres in Hole J-62-26, including 551 g/t gold over 1 metre. The 100% hit rate across the new batch — in a program now past 12,900 metres total — sent shares up 31% on the day; true widths have not yet been determined.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR BIDS 92% PREMIUM FOR NOBLE PLAINS — Binding LOI Targets Wyoming Powder River Basin Uranium in All-Stock Deal
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy (NASDAQ: NUCL) signed a binding letter of intent on November 4 to acquire Noble Plains Uranium in an all-stock deal pricing each Noble Plains share at CAD $0.125 — a 92% premium to the last close — with Eagle shareholders retaining approximately 95% of the combined entity. The deal targets the Duck Creek uranium project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin and the Shirley Central project; a shareholder vote is expected Q1 2027 and a reciprocal break fee of US$400,000 applies.

headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 COMBINATION CLOSES — 388M Ag-Eq Oz Combined; 'Made In America' Silver Miner Lists as Bunker Hill Silver Corp.
snippet: The Bunker Hill Mining and Silver47 Exploration combination closes on or about November 5 following shareholder approval on October 28, creating a US-focused silver and critical minerals producer that will trade as Bunker Hill Silver Corp. on the TSX. The combined entity holds 80 million silver-equivalent ounces in measured and indicated resources and 308 million in inferred across four primary US projects — Bunker Hill, Red Mountain, Hughes, and Mogollon — anchored by US$20M in concurrent financing.

headline: LUNDIN'S RECORD COPPER QUARTER — $1.1B Revenue at $6.85/lb Realized; Vicuna FID Targeted Year-End Despite Caserones Storm Cuts
snippet: Lundin Mining (TSX: LUN) reported Q3 2026 revenue of US$1.1 billion — its fourth consecutive billion-dollar quarter — driven by a record realized copper price of $6.85 per pound on 62,610 tonnes of copper production, with free cash flow of approximately $418M. Full-year Caserones guidance was cut to 105,000–115,000 tonnes following winter storms in Chile, while the Vicuña copper district in Argentina spent US$81M in the quarter as the company targets a Stage 1 final investment decision before year-end.

headline: RUSSIA'S URANIUM GRIP IS BIGGER THAN MARKETS KNOW — Think Tank: Hidden Contracts and Niger Control Could Squeeze Western Supply
snippet: A think-tank report released November 5 argues that Russia's strategic position in global uranium supply is substantially larger than production figures imply, citing undisclosed off-take arrangements, state-owned processing infrastructure, and ongoing competition for African deposits including Niger — where Moscow and Washington are both maneuvering for influence. The report calls for accelerated long-term Western contracting and domestic uranium production development as the only credible structural response.

headline: COPPER SHANGHAI PREMIUM HITS 2.5-YEAR HIGH — $14,058/t LME Holds Post-Midterms as China Physical Tightness Bites
snippet: Copper on the London Metal Exchange stabilized above $14,058 per tonne on November 5 as the post-midterm dollar weakness added a fresh tailwind, while Shanghai's spot copper premium over futures climbed to 1,900 yuan per tonne — the highest level since 2021 — signalling acute near-term physical supply tightness in China that the LME futures curve has not yet priced. The divergence between spot physical demand and paper futures positions is a classic early signal of a coming forward curve squeeze.

headline: MP MATERIALS FACES Q3 RECKONING TODAY — NdPr Forecast Above 1,000 MT But Stock at 16-Month Low Ahead of After-Close Print
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reports Q3 2026 results after the closing bell on November 5, with Wall Street's consensus calling for $117.55M in revenue and NdPr production exceeding 1,000 metric tonnes — building on Q2's 840 MT and Q1's record 917 MT. The stock enters earnings day at 16-month lows after falling 53% from its 52-week high, with investors watching guidance language on critical minerals policy under the new Democratic majority for any re-rating catalyst.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL: Q3 DEMAND HOLDS AT 1,369 TONNES — ETF Holdings Reach Record 4,256t as Institutions Return in Scale
snippet: Total global gold demand edged down just 1% year-on-year to 1,369 tonnes in Q3 2026, according to a World Gold Council report summarized by Money Metals on November 3, with ETF gold holdings climbing to a record 4,256 tonnes as institutional investors returned in size alongside persistent central bank buying. The demand floor from sovereign buyers — combined with ETF accumulation — underpins the structural bull case for gold even as prices pulled back from the January 2026 high of $5,595.

headline: SILVER'S INDUSTRIAL CASE EXPANDS — Fuel Cell Catalysts and Cheaper Nanoparticles Open New Demand Channels as 67M Oz Deficit Looms
snippet: New manufacturing techniques are cutting silver nanoparticle production costs and unlocking commercial applications in hydrogen fuel cell catalysts, next-generation semiconductor packaging, and antimicrobial coatings, according to a November 3 Money Metals analysis. With the Silver Institute projecting a 67 million ounce structural supply deficit in 2026 and silver sitting roughly 55% below its year high near $120, the growing industrial demand story is a data point the investment case didn't fully price at the peak.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO EXPANDS TO HIGH 70s — Analyst: Silver Oversold at $49 Support; Mean Reversion Setup Building
snippet: A GoldSeek contributor argues the gold-silver ratio has widened to the high 70s — up from roughly 72 just weeks ago — as silver's correction from $120 to near $49 outpaced gold's pullback from $5,595, leaving silver technically oversold at a key support level near $49.56. The analysis identifies a mean-reversion trade back toward the 65–70 range as the highest-probability outcome if gold stabilizes above $4,000, with the GDX miners ETF also flagged as undervalued relative to the metal.
